correctness.rationale: For each non-induced injective embedding, fix its e required edges; the incident degree at each image vertex is d_v+Bin(n−1−d_v,p), all outside vertices retain their binomial degrees. Covariance linearity yields the normalized finite formula for all n,h,k,p. After cancelling isolated motif vertices, the sign function is strictly decreasing; its limits at 0 and 1 and the maximum-degree endpoint yield the complete strict classification. An induced P3 fixes its chord absent and alters the endpoint law to 1+Bin(n−3,p), yielding a quadratic with two roots exactly when n≥4. A standalone rational checker enumerates all graphs on 3–5 vertices for five p values, six hundred exact tests plus boundary assertions (608 total). Enumeration does not replace the universal algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: Compared actual published research-index searches and accessible overlapping mathematical claims for equations, objects and implication; none contains degree-class count versus arbitrary motif-count covariance or the induced 3-path two-switch contrast. Primary full-text comparisons: fixed-degree-sequence subgraph expectations (arXiv:1801.09813), graphon subgraph fluctuations (arXiv:2104.07259), and Erdős–Rényi two-vertex degree law (arXiv:2303.05138). Earlier conditional mixed moments remain possible and independent historical-priority verification is outstanding.
residual_risks: The conditional-moment proof is elementary; the full all-motif sign classification may be an unlabelled corollary of an earlier bivariate generating function or subgraph-degree census.

value.rationale: Degree frequencies and motif counts are natural statistics of the same G(n,p) model. The result classifies signs simultaneously for all vertex degrees, graph motifs including disconnected motifs, all n and all edge densities, making a useful qualitative deduction from a finite exact identity. The induced/non-induced distinction has a sharp natural four-vertex onset and two explicit reentrant thresholds, demonstrating a substantive structural boundary rather than a narrow numerical instance. No paper-sized generalization or downstream application is needed for this classification.
